business_problem: Sinocare was rolling out multiple AI applications for chronic-disease management, including periodic assessment, anomaly analysis, glycemic prediction, diet imaging, and diet guidance, but it had to connect several model vendors at once. Different API protocols, authentication schemes, and response formats slowed launches and forced repeated adapter work, while healthcare compliance demanded unified audit logs, centralized permissions, and safety controls that fragmented model calls could not provide.
solution_summary: Sinocare built a governed multi-model AI delivery layer on Alibaba Cloud AI Gateway. The gateway standardizes access to external and custom models through a single API plane, automatically normalizing authentication, protocol, and response differences so application teams can switch or add models without hard-coded rewrites. Around that entry point, Sinocare enabled consumer authentication, rate limiting, circuit-breaking, and fallback so chronic-disease applications can continue serving users even when a preferred model is throttled or unavailable. The gateway also enforces AI safety guardrails and captures full request or answer logs for auditability, which matters when health-related prompts and outputs must be governed under medical compliance requirements. AI Gateway also sends QPS, token, latency, and error telemetry into Cloud Monitor 2.0 so Sinocare can tune performance, attribute cost, and alert on anomalies across its multi-model AI estate.

solution_components.name: AI Gateway
solution_components.role: Provides the standardized multi-model access layer, routing, fallback, guardrails, and audit logging for Sinocare's healthcare AI applications.

solution_components.name: Cloud Monitor 2.0
solution_components.role: Collects latency, QPS, token, and error metrics so the team can operate the AI estate with visibility and alerting.

data_flow: Sinocare's AI applications send requests through AI Gateway, which authenticates the caller, normalizes model-specific protocols, applies safety checks, selects the target model, and records request or answer logs for audit. Telemetry about latency, tokens, throughput, and failure conditions then flows into Cloud Monitor 2.0 for visualization, alerting, and cost or performance analysis.
business_outcome: Sinocare replaced fragmented model integrations with a single governed AI operating plane. The standard API layer eliminated repeated adapter development, reduced model-switching work from weeks to hours, and raised AI application launch speed by 50% while adding the audit, content-safety, and observability controls needed for healthcare compliance.
metrics: products are distributed in 187 countries and regions
single model changes fell from weeks to hours
architecture_clues: AI Gateway is used as a protocol-convergence layer so business applications do not hard-code vendor-specific API logic.
The gateway applies API Key, JWT, and HMAC-style controls together with multi-dimensional rate limiting and fallback.
Full question, answer, and context logging is treated as a healthcare audit requirement, not just an observability feature.
Cloud Monitor 2.0 becomes the unified telemetry layer for request volume, latency, token use, and error-rate alerts.
